messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-ml — multi-GPU job group 'tp-run-42' failing fast, repeated communicator timeouts reported. Root cause unknown. Logs attached in thread.
alex_m: saw the page, jumping in. what's the customer impact?
sam_cs: customer-rep on slack — 15% of requests to their inference endpoint are 500'ing, latency spikes to >6s for other requests. They just flagged degraded production.
rachel_sre: can you paste the failing log lines? I got an alert for repeated Xid errors from the node (xid 79) a few mins ago.
devin_runtime: pasting tail from the runtime container logs:
```
[2026-03-15T21:47:10Z] ERROR runtime: nccl allreduce timeout, step=8345, rank=3
[2026-03-15T21:47:10Z] ERROR runtime: cuda error: device-side assert triggered (Xid 79)
[2026-03-15T21:47:11Z] WARN runtime: lost communicator 0x7f9b3c due to timeout
[2026-03-15T21:47:12Z] INFO orchestrator: container restart requested for pod tp-run-42-3
```
mira_infra: that node (gpu-node-14) shows a kernel OOPS and NVLINK resets around the same time. I'm seeing a container crashloop on that pod.
alex_m: rank 3 = gpu-node-14, correct?
devin_runtime: yes. Also the KV-cache warmup failed and subsequent requests stall waiting on rendezvous.
leon_p: I can take oncall for the next 30min, handing over to rachel after if needed. @rachel_sre you good to take next?
rachel_sre: taking after leon. for now leon, run the immediate mitigations.
leon_p: ok. immediate plan: 1) cordon gpu-node-14, 2) drain and restart pods, 3) force fallback to single-GPU replica for critical customer route, 4) open bridge if customer impact persists. executing step 1 now.
deploy-bot: Cordon command executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-14` (ok)
leon_p: draining now, will allow evict with grace 30s for faster turn. `kubectl drain gpu-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --force --grace-period=30`
deploy-bot: Eviction started, pod tp-run-42-3 -> terminating
devin_runtime: while draining, change runtime policy to prefer replicating to other nodes and disable collective scheduling for this job: toggling `serve.runtime.collectives.enabled=false` for the job id. patching now.
leon_p: patched, confirming workers will re-register with new config.
mira_infra: node shows ECC corrected errors increasing before OOPS; NVLINK serr intermittently. I'm putting node into maintenance and requesting replacement GPU.
sam_cs: informed customer that degraded performance is happening and we're running mitigation (node drain and fallback). told them estimated recovery 10-20m.
alex_m: after drain, are other ranks healthy? any evidence of split-brain?
devin_runtime: remaining ranks show elevated allreduce latency but not full deadlock. however, KV-cache sync stalled for several seqs, caused queued requests to back up. fallback to single-GPU path will let those succeed.
leon_p: container restarted on node gpu-node-19 with rank reassigned, initial smoke shows endpoint returning 200s again for some requests.
deploy-bot: Canary traffic rerouted to single-gpu variant for route /v1/serve/customers/42 (10% -> 100% now)
alex_m: good. keep an eye on token generation latencies — single-GPU will increase per-request time but reduce error rate.
devin_runtime: adding additional guard: set NCCL timeout to 3000ms for cluster to reduce transient disconnects while we stabilize. patching cluster config.
nathan_ops: (reacts :thumbsup:) — note: we should capture coredump and nv-support logs before the node replacement. Mira, can you coordinate?
mira_infra: yes, collecting `dmesg`, `nvidia-bug-report` and kernel-wedge logs now, will upload to internal storage and attach link.
leon_p: monitoring metrics: error rate for customer route down from 15% -> 2% after fallback and restarts. latency median up from 120ms -> 420ms. still acceptable for now per customer SLA fallback.
sam_cs: customer replied: "Thanks — reduced errors, service acceptable for now. Keep us posted."
alex_m: next steps: 1) preserve node logs & telemetry for postmortem, 2) replace GPU on node-14, 3) validate NVLINK stability after replacement, 4) consider increasing NCCL watchdog/backoff for short term. assign owners?
mira_infra: I'll coordinate hardware replacement and artifact upload (owner: mira_infra).
devin_runtime: I'll work on short-term runtime config (NCCL timeouts, fallback policies) and create a canary to test multi-gpu collectives after replacement (owner: devin_runtime).
leon_p: I'll assemble incident timeline and run initial severity assessment, will update incident channel with customer impact summary in 30m.
deploy-bot: Postmortem template created: https://internal/redwood/incidents/postmortem/new?incident=4423109876
alex_m: thanks team. please add any additional logs or anomalies here. rachel, handing off to you for the follow-up and post-incident review.
rachel_sre: taking it. I'll keep the incident open until NVLINK verified and postmortem drafted. marking severity P1 due to customer error rate spike and multi-GPU comms instability.
inc-bot: Incident 4423109876 status: mitigated -> partial; channel will remain open for follow-up.
leon_p: quick note for postmortem: check for coroutines holding tensor references across allreduce calls (we've seen that cause stray device asserts in the past). also look at scheduler packing for this job class.
devin_runtime: logging that. grabbing run-level artifacts now.
mira_infra: uploaded artifacts: https://internal/storage/incident-4423109876/artifacts (dmesg, nvrpt, container logs)
leon_p: thanks — closing active pager. will continue with replacement and postmortem.
sam_cs: closing customer loop with summary and ETA for full recovery.
inc-bot: Pager cleared for incident 4423109876.
